newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Podravka makes '95 loss, seeks equity cut.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Podravka makes '95 loss, seeks equity cut.

text.p: Croatian food-processing firm Podravka said on Friday it turned to a 1995 group loss of 135.3 million kuna, from a profit of 58.4 million a year earlier.
In its annual report, the company blamed the strong kuna, which had put a lid on exports, depressed food prices and production losses at some of its subsidiaries for the loss.
Podravka also said it was seeking a 124 million German marks capital cut after auditors found its 1995 group balance sheet of three billion kuna was overvalued by 370 million kuna.
"It is not realistic...," said Ante Babic, head of Podravka's restructuring team. "For two years we've been discussing this with the (Croatian) Privatisation Fund."
The government controls around 55 percent of Podravka through the Croatian Privatisation Fund and two pension funds while private shareholders hold the rest.
Podravka now asked the fund to reduce its 34-percent holding and increase the private investors' share accordingly.

A similar capital reduction was applied last year to drug maker Pliva, which was then privatised through an international offering. The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) later bought an 11 percent equity stake in the company.

Babic said Podravka expected to get the government's final ruling this month and would submit the plan to its shareholders at the annual meeting scheduled for September 27. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
